newsitem.title: CANADA: Suncor to build Alberta oil sands pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Suncor to build Alberta oil sands pipeline.

text.p: Suncor Inc said on Wednesday it planned to build a C$250 million pipeline to the Hardisty area, southeast of Edmonton, Alberta from its oil sands operation near Fort McMurray, Alberta.
Suncor said the 530-kilometer pipeline would provide access to new markets and give the company added flexibility to deliver a variety of products to consumers.
"The Athabasca pipeline is part of Suncor's plans to expand its oil sands and heavy oil operations," Suncor president and chief executive Rick George said.
Suncor's oil sands plant is expected to be producing 105,000 barrels a day by 1999, up from current production of 79,500, Suncor said.
It said construction is slated to begin in the summer of 1997 and be completed in late 1998.
The proposed 24-inch pipeline will initially have the capacity to ship 55,000 barrels a day, and capacity can be expanded as Suncor's production grows.

The company currently operates a synthetic crude pipeline between Fort McMurray and Edmonton. It said the new pipeline will complement the existing operation and enable Suncor to ship a wider offering of custom blended products to its customers.
Suncor said the pipeline will have potential links with other pipeline systems including Interprovincial Pipe Line Inc and Express Pipeline Ltd.
It said the route to Hardisty has not been finalized.
